dhp1:1: These verses describe a threefold process: intention, actions, and consequences. Each of these three “things” is included under dhammā. This line is phrased in prose at AN 1.56–7; see there for further notes. | Mano here is the active aspect of mind, effectively meaning kamma. Translating as “mind” obscures the ethical reading in favor of an idealistic one, which given the remainder of the verse is unjustified. | The MS edition on which this translation is based has headings for each of the verses. These are derived from the background stories told in the commentary. As such, I have not translated them as they are not intrinsic to the text.
dhp1:3: Intention is expressed through actions of speech and body.
dhp1:5: The consequence of bad actions is suffering. In popular culture, the consequence is often said to be kamma, but in early Buddhism, kamma is the action that creates the consequence.
